me:2016:q12-s3.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 3 | Question: 12
me:2016:q12-s3.question: Which of the bearings given below SHOULD NOT be subjected to a thrust load?

detailed_solution.concept: Machine Design - Rolling Contact Bearings & Load Capacities
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Bearing Topologies & Load Carrying Capabilities:**
  - Rolling element bearings are designed for specific load directions:
    1. **Deep Groove Ball Bearings:**
       - Deep raceways accommodate high radial loads and moderate axial (thrust) loads in either direction.
    2. **Angular Contact Ball Bearings:**
       - Contact angle between raceways and balls is inclined ($15^\circ$ to $40^\circ$), allowing them to carry heavy combined radial and single-direction axial (thrust) loads.
    3. **Tapered Roller Bearings:**
       - Conical raceways and rollers are inclined at an angle, designed specifically for heavy combined radial and unidirectional thrust loads.
    4. **Cylindrical (Straight) Roller Bearings:**
       - Cylindrical rollers provide line contact along parallel cylindrical raceways, conferring exceptional radial load carrying capacity and rigidity.
       - However, straight cylindrical rollers have flat ends that provide no contact angle for axial reaction forces. Any axial thrust force results in metal-to-metal rubbing/sliding friction against guiding flanges, causing severe overheating, skidding, and premature seizure.
       - Therefore, straight cylindrical roller bearings **SHOULD NOT be subjected to a thrust load**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (Cylindrical (straight) roller bearing)**.

The area wherein discharge takes place gets heated to very high temperature such that the surface get melted & removed. The cut particles (debris) get flushed away by continuous flowing dielectric fluid. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

Ch. equation is $|A-\lambda I|=0$

$(2-\lambda)(2-\lambda)(3-\lambda)=0$

$\lambda=2,2,3$

$\lambda=3$ there is one L.I. Eigen vector

$\lambda=2 \quad$Consider $(A-2 I) x=0$

$\text{rank} =2 \quad$ The equation are $x_{2}=0$

No. of variables $=3 x_{3}=0$

Let $x_{1}=k$ be independent.

$$\therefore \text{Eigen vector is}\; \left[\begin{array}{l}k \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]=k\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$$

Only one independent Eigen vector in the case of

$\lambda=2$

Hence finally no. of L.I. Eigen vectors =2

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

me:2016:q39-s3.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 3 | Question: 39
me:2016:q39-s3.question: Consider a fully developed steady laminar flow of an incompressible fluid with viscosity $\mu$ through a circular pipe of radius R. primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown: Shear stress at the wall, $\tau_{0}=\tau_{\max }=\frac{k \mu U_{1}}{R}$ We know that the velocity at any point for laminar flow through pipe, $$\begin{aligned} u&=-\frac{1}{4 \mu}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right)\left(R^{2}-r^{2}\right)\\ \mathrm{At} \quad r&=\frac{R}{2}, u=U_{1}\\ \therefore \quad U_{1} &=-\frac{1}{4 \mu}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right)\left(R^{2}-\frac{R^{2}}{4}\right) \\ &=-\frac{1}{4 \mu}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right) \frac{3}{4} R^{2} \\ &=-\frac{3}{16 \mu}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right) R^{2}\\ \therefore \tau_{0}&=-\frac{K \mu}{R} \times \frac{3}{16 \mu}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right) R^{2}\\ \tau_{0}&=-\frac{3}{16} K\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right) R\\ \end{aligned}$$ We know that maximum shear stress at wall. $\tau_{0}=-\frac{R \partial p}{\partial} \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ $\therefore-\frac{3}{16} K\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right) R=-\frac{R}{2} \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ $\text{or}K=\frac{8}{3}=2.66$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2.65** (acceptable range: [2.6, 2.7]).

me:2016:q41-s3.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 3 | Question: 41
me:2016:q41-s3.question:
For a two-dimensional flow, the velocity field is $\vec{u}=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\hat{i}+\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\hat{j}$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are the basis vectors in the x-y Cartesian coordinate system. Identify the CORRECT statements from below.
(1)The flow is incompressible
(2)The flow is unsteady.
(3) y-component of acceleration, $a_{y}=\frac{-y}{(x^{2}+y^{2})^{2}}$
(4) x-component of acceleration,$a_{x}=\frac{-(x+y)}{(x^{2}+y^{2})^{2}}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
For $2 \mathrm{D}$ -flow velocity field is:

$$\begin{aligned} \vec{V}&=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \hat{i}+\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \hat{j}\\ so \quad u&=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} and v=\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \\ a_{x} &=u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+v \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} \\ &=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left[\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right] \\ &+\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left[\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right] \\ &= \frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\left[\frac{x(-2 x)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}}+\frac{1}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right]\\ &+\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \left[\frac{x(2 y)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}}\right]\\ &=\frac{-2 x^{3}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}+\frac{x}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}}\\ &+ \frac{2xy^{2}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}\\ &=\frac{-2 x^{3}+x\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)-2 x y^{2}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}} \\ &=\frac{-2 x^{3}+x^{3}+x y^{2}-2 x y^{2}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}\\ &=\frac{-x^{3}-x y^{2}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}} \\ &=\frac{-x\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} a_{x} &=\frac{x}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ a_{y} &=u \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}+u \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} \\ &=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left[\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right] \\& +\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left[\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right] \\ &=\frac{x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \frac{(-2 x y)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}}\\& +\frac{y}{x^{2}+y^{2}} \times\left[\frac{-2 y^{2}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}}+\frac{1}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\right]\\ &=\frac{-2 x^{2} y}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}+\frac{2 y^{3}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}\\&+\frac{y}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{-2 x^{2} y-2 y^{3}+y\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}} \\ &=\frac{-x^{2} y-y^{3}}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}}=\frac{y\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{3}} \\ a_{y}&=\frac{-y}{\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} T_{e} &=260 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{c} &=310 \mathrm{K} \\ c_{p l} &=4.8 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ h_{fg} &=1054 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \text { at } T_{c}=310 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Taking reference temperature T , at which entropy is $s_{T}$ $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad s_{3}-s_{T} &=c \ln \frac{T_{3}}{T} \\ s_{3} &=s_{T}+c \ln \frac{T_{3}}{T}=s_{T}+4.8 \ln \frac{310}{T} \\ \text { Similarly, } s_{0} &=s_{T}+c \ln \frac{260}{T}=s_{T}+4.8 \ln \frac{260}{T} \\ \therefore \quad s_{2}-s_{3} &=\frac{h_{f g}}{T}=\frac{1054}{310} \\ s_{2} &=s_{3}+\frac{1054}{310} \end{aligned}$$ Substitute the value of $s_{3}$ in above equation, we get $$\begin{aligned} s_{2} &=s_{T}+4.8 \ln \frac{310}{T}+\frac{1054}{310} \\ s_{2} &=s_{1} \\ s_{1} &=s_{T}+4.8 \ln \frac{310}{T}+\frac{1054}{310} \\ h_{1}-h_{0} &=T_{e}\left[s_{1}-s_{0}\right] \\ =& 260 \times\left[s_{T}+4.8 \ln \frac{310}{T}+\frac{1054}{310}\right.\\ &\left.-s_{T}-4.8 \ln \frac{260}{T}\right] \\ &=260\left[4.8 \ln \left(\frac{310}{T} \times \frac{T}{260}\right)+\frac{1054}{310}\right] \\ &1103.51\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1112.5** (acceptable range: [1095, 1130]).

detailed_solution.markdown: The question will be solved using the graphical method $\text{Maximize } Z=40X_1+100X_2$ Constraints are $$\begin{aligned} 12X_1+6X_2 \leq 6000 \\ 4X_1+10X_2 \leq 4000 \\ 2X_1+3X_2 \leq 1800 \\ X_1,X_2 \geq 0 \end{aligned}$$ We have three corner points as follow $$\begin{aligned} \text{At }(0,400)\;\;\;&Z=40,000\\ \text{At }(375,250)\;\;\;&Z=40,000\\ \text{At }(500,100)\;\;\;&Z=20,000 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, maximum profit per week is 40,000.
